parsed.hook: Ramnista comes off 30–40 year-old Xinomavro vines rooted in Naoussa’s rusty limestone; that soil is the reason a 2015 can smell like sun-warmed brick and sour cherry at the same time. At ~$29 it’s the cheapest ticket to northern Greece’s answer to Barolo tannin without the Piemonte mark-up.
parsed.wine_summary: Kir Yianni was carved out of the old Boutari family empire in 1997 and immediately focused on replanting Xinomavro at 200–300 m on the Vermio foothills where limestone bedrock keeps pH low—exactly what the variety needs to guard its sky-high acidity. Naoussa is legally 100 % Xinomavro, so Ramnista can’t hide behind blending; instead the estate ages the wine 14 months in 30 % new French barriques and gives it another year in 3,000-L Slavonian casks, a split that softens seed tannin but still leaves the grape’s tell-tale tomato-leaf aroma intact. The result is a wine that carries 13.5 % alcohol yet can clock in with total acidity above 7 g/L—numbers that translate into bright, transparent fruit and the structural grip that makes Nebbiolo comparisons unavoidable.
parsed.terroir_expression: Naoussa sits on the uplifted Mesohellenic Trough: fractured limestone mixed with iron-rich clay that turns brick-red when dry. That porosity forces roots to dive 2–3 m for water, shrinking berry size and thickening skins; you taste it as a burst of sour-cherry flavour and a drying, powdered-clay finish that mirrors the scent of a wet terracotta roof.
parsed.vinification_summary: After a 20-day maceration—long for a thin-skinned variety—malolactic is blocked until spring, keeping total SO₂ low and primary fruit vivid. The dual-barrel regimen (new French for mid-palate creaminess, neutral Slavonian for oxygen micro-exchange) knocks the edges off Xinomavro’s notoriously spiky tannins without sanding away the variety’s iron-tinged backbone.
parsed.food_pairing: 1) Nashville hot chicken sandwich: the acid cuts the fry-oil while tannins grab the cayenne crust. 2) Tagliatelle al ragù Bolognese: tomato acidity mirrors the wine’s, and the meat fat softens tannin. 3) Grilled lamb chop with oregano and lemon: herbal overlap plus high acid refreshes the fat. 4) Mushroom & thyme pide: earth on earth, with cheese buffering the firm structure.
parsed.comparable_wines: Produttori del Barbaresco Langhe Nebbiolo — same acid-tannin seesaw and sour-cherry core without new-oak gloss. Château Musar Jeune — another limestone-grown, high-acid Mediterranean red that leans on savory spice. Canalicchio di Sopra Rosso di Montalcino — similarly transparent, medium-bodied and built for acids-first food pairing.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied dry red with high acidity and iron-laced tannin
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink 2015–2022 now; 2012–2013 can sleep to 2028 if stored at 55 °F. Older vintages shut down hard around year six—give them 30 minutes in a decanter.
parsed.value_assessment: $29 at Spec’s lines up next to Langhe Nebbiolo in the low-$30s and basic Crozes-Hermitage at $28–32; Ramnista outruns both for aging upside because Greek pricing still lags its quality curve.
parsed.market_position: You’ll spot it on Greek restaurant lists in NYC and Chicago by the glass—somms use it as their “Nebbiolo for $55 on the list” play. Retail turnover is slower outside metro areas, so 2015s still sit on shelves while Napa Cab of the same price sold through years ago.
parsed.insider_take: Most shoppers reach for Assyrtiko when they buy Greek; Xinomavro is the better sleeper. Ramnista’s only real risk is bottle variation—limestone + high acid can throw crusty tartrate clouds that freak out casual drinkers, but the wine underneath is sound.
